method: bounded search of Europe PMC REST (search + core abstracts + fullTextXML for open-access papers) and the arXiv export API on 2026-10-04 (scratchpad file times 02:19:56-02:26:06 +0800 for the retrieved texts; Europe PMC searches ran in the same window); passages below were read in the retrieved text (abstract or full text as stated). Absence of prior art is 'not found in a bounded search', never proof of absence. Earlier verified sources (WS4 literature_verification.json) are reused where stated.
overall: None of the study's candidate contributions is methodologically new. Budget allocation between screening and confirmation, adaptive combination screening, replication/reproducibility modelling, and time-uniform or conformal certificates all have primary prior art. What is not found: an equal-budget, independently verified comparison of verification-allocation schedulers in combination screens, and the use of a predicted independent-confirmation probability to allocate verification. Those would be empirical/application contributions, conditional on a qualified dataset (none exists; data_qualification.json).

claims.claim: Allocating a fixed budget between screening new candidates, paying for independent verification of hits, and stopping

prior_art.ref: Satagopan JM, Elston RC. Optimal two-stage genotyping in population-based association studies. Genet Epidemiol 2003
prior_art.passage: all markers are tested at stage 1 on a subset of samples and the most promising are genotyped on the remaining individuals at stage 2; parameters chosen to minimise cost at fixed overall significance and power; the two-stage procedure typically halves the cost of the study

prior_art.ref: Skol AD, Scott LJ, Abecasis GR, Boehnke M. Joint analysis is more efficient than replication-based analysis for two-stage genome-wide association studies. Nat Genet 2006
prior_art.passage: staged designs genotype a proportion of samples in stage 1 and follow up a proportion of markers in stage 2; joint analysis of both stages is more powerful than treating stage 2 as a replication study

prior_art.ref: Woo HM, Qian X, Tan L, Jha S, Alexander FJ, Dougherty ER, Yoon BJ. Optimal decision-making in high-throughput virtual screening pipelines. Patterns 2023
prior_art.passage: optimally allocate computational resources to multi-fidelity stages to maximise return on computational investment; the per-stage screening threshold is the decision variable; non-linear (DAG) pipelines are named as open

prior_art.ref: Binois M, Huang J, Gramacy RB, Ludkovski M. Replication or exploration? Sequential design for stochastic simulation experiments. Technometrics 2019
prior_art.passage: a lookahead sequential design decides whether a new run should replicate an existing input or explore a new one, with a heteroskedastic GP learning signal and noise

prior_art.ref: Wu Z, Liu D, Sui Y. Quantitative assessment of hit detection and confirmation in single and duplicate high-throughput screenings. J Biomol Screen 2008
prior_art.passage: in most assays only compounds selected in primary screening are followed up in confirmation experiments; confirmation-rate estimation from a primary score is proposed

claims.residual: the specific instance (anchored combination screens; verification = a second orientation on disjoint plates; per-line equal-budget comparison with physical charging) was not found; an empirical result there is a replication of a known design principle in a new setting
